title: Public-pension funding pressure can shape private-equity matching and the productivity of financed firms
source_unit: Census CES working paper linking U.S. public-pension investments, private-equity funds, target firms, and confidential Census firm data
geography: United States public pensions, private-equity funds, and financed firms

observations.period: Public-pension private-equity investments and financed-firm outcomes; paper published July 2026

denominator.unit: U.S. public pensions, private-equity funds, and target firms in linked investment and Census data; exact public abstract denominator not disclosed

pension_funding_and_returns.value: more severely underfunded public pensions receive lower average private-equity returns

general_partner_matching.value: more severely underfunded pensions match with smaller general partners on average

financed_firm_productivity.value: firms financed by the most underfunded pensions and smallest private-equity funds face labor-productivity decreases

identification_context.value: public unionization is used as an instrument related to pension underfunding positions

observations.method: Census CES working paper traces public-pension private-equity investments to target firms using private-investment microdata linked with confidential Census data; it uses public unionization as an instrument supporting the underfunding position and evaluates alternate mechanisms.
observations.uncertainty: This is a Census working paper and has not undergone the review and editorial process of an official Census publication. The public abstract does not disclose all sample construction, return definitions, fund-selection details, effect sizes, or productivity measures. The reported patterns do not by themselves establish effects on pension beneficiaries, employment, wages, firm survival, or public budgets.
observations.subgroup: Public pensions differentiated by funding status, private-equity funds differentiated by general-partner size, and firms financed by those funds.
observations.counterinterpretation: Underfunding, fund size, returns, and productivity may be jointly shaped by pension governance, risk tolerance, investment policy, firm selection, sector, macro conditions, or unmeasured fund quality. A productivity decrease does not identify whether workers lost jobs, wages, hours, control, or security.

boundary: This record adds a public-pension-to-private-equity-to-firm-productivity pathway. It does not establish pension solvency, beneficiary security, worker harm, firm failure, or whether a different investment policy would improve public outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Census working-paper landing page reviewed; private-investment and confidential Census firm microdata are not retained
